Jira has always been very quick and responsive for me. It offers a good amount of customization too... I've never felt that jira has been a limiting factor of what the teams I've been on have wanted to do with our workflow. Never once encountered a major bug in it either.
That said, Jira does have it downsides, and not tracking dependencies very well is one of them.
Biggest problem when I used it, could not assign anything to more than 1 person.

I personally find Jira miles more confusing than Radar after having used both extensively... as a native application, it showed tickets in a regular table view where you could multi-select, drag and drop, etc.

For me a particularly frustrating aspect is the way the UI moves around a lot. I'm quite anxious to click anything until all the loading spinners have stopped... Also it's really annoying when I try to copy something from a ticket description but it starts editing the whole description field.

As a developer, once I finish my ticket I assign it to a QA. Then I can never get back to the ticket. I'd like a really easy way to see all of the tickets I've ever completed. But completed tickets aren't assigned to me, they're assigned to QA.

I came from Apple (and their excellent Radar issue tracking tool) to a company that uses Jira. Jira is the worst. I routinely lose data in jira, like saving errors. Dragging and dropping attachments sometimes causes the page to crash and reload.

Single letter hotkeys are pretty bad. If it's not an input field you've focused but the page itself, you might assign the ticket to yourself and set it to some crazy state before you realize the focus is all wrong.
Once a JIRA shop, we moved everything to Asana years ago... Our design team just could not get on board with JIRA. It was too much 'work,' in their words, to track their efforts.

Jira drives me crazy. Why do I need to mark an epic as closed two different ways? Why is it really difficult to see what tickets were in a closed sprint? Why is it so slow or why does it sometimes get in infinite reload loop? Features randomly break like the ability to create tickets from confluence.
Due to the slow loading, I ended up writing some simple Jira API wrapper scripts for submitting bug reports quicker in our systems.
Trying to do something as seemingly simple as create a useful saved search in JIRA is so painful I can't imagine its creation was not an act of sabotage.
Jira is bloated. Full stop. It feels like there isn't a strong unified product vision for Jira. It's just trying to solve everything.

One of the things I like most about Jira is the ability to execute useful queries via REST on the data stored in there. Most of the times when I read some post about Jira alternatives is that they completely ignore this topic.
Please, kill Jira and Confluence. I hate Atlassian tools so much. The user interfaces are sluggish no matter the hardware you're using... it's a shame it became almost a standard in our industry.

My opinion based on feature and screenshots is that the UX is as shitty as Jira. The nightmare with Jira is this product manager obsession with kanban boards that become overwhelmed once your project become serious.
Does Plane offer an alternative for JQL (Jira Query Language)? That's what I appreciate most about Jira.
